stem: An endowment fund pays Rs 12,000 every year forever. The discount rate is 8% per annum. What is the present value of this perpetuity?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student uses 12.5% as denominator instead of 8%: 12,000 / 0.125 = 96,000.
PV of perpetuity = PMT / r = 12,000 / 0.08 = Rs 1,50,000.
Student uses 10% instead of 8% as the discount rate: 12,000 / 0.10 = 1,20,000.
Student treats 8% of 12,000 as the present value and multiplies by an incorrect factor of 10, giving Rs 1,00,000.

explanation: Present value of a perpetuity = PMT / r. With PMT = 12,000 and r = 0.08: PV = 12,000 / 0.08 = Rs 1,50,000. A common error is using the wrong discount rate or applying a finite-period formula.

explanation_sections.punchline: For a perpetuity, PV = PMT / r. Rs 12,000 divided by 0.08 equals Rs 1,50,000.
explanation_sections.approach: Recognise the word "forever" or "in perpetuity" as the signal to use PV = PMT / r. There is no n and no annuity table needed. Convert the discount rate from percentage to decimal before dividing. The calculation is a single division.
explanation_sections.lesson: A perpetuity has only one formula: PMT divided by the decimal rate. Applying a finite-period annuity formula or using the wrong rate are the only two ways to go wrong here.
explanation_sections.timing: About 60 seconds. This is an L1 item. The division 12,000 / 0.08 = 1,50,000 takes 10 seconds. Reject option (1) in five seconds: that would require a rate of 10%, not 8%.
